# phoxal_api - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/phoxal-api/0.19.3/target-redirect/phoxal_api/

## Expand description

The single API layer (D60/D61).

This crate is the dated API contract tree. It depends only on the
[ phoxal-bus](https://docs.rs/phoxal-bus/0.20.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_bus/index.html) ABI floor (the contract primitive traits and the
typed-topic builders) and the

[proc-macros; it does](https://docs.rs/phoxal-macros/0.19.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_macros/index.html)

`phoxal-macros`**not**depend on the

`phoxal` engine. A participant depends on both crates
and imports the API tree directly with `use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`, so
`phoxal_api::y2026_1`, `phoxal_api::ApiVersion`, and `phoxal_api::ContractBody`
are the canonical paths.[§](https://docs.rs#dated-api-versions)Dated API versions

An API version is a **dated module** (`phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …) generated by
[ phoxal_api_tree!](https://docs.rs/phoxal-macros/0.19.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_macros/macro.phoxal_api_tree.html). Each version module carries:

- a zero-variant marker `enum Api {}`implementing`ApiVersion``ApiVersion::ID``"y2026_1"`);
- the version-local wire bodies, one `pub mod`per contract node holding plain serde structs/enums and their`ContractBody`
- an api-local `topic`builder rooted at`topic::new()`.

Versions can build on earlier ones with `version y2026_2 extends y2026_1`:
every inherited node and type is re-emitted *fresh* under the new module - same
[ ContractBody::FAMILY](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.FAMILY) and

[, a different](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.TOPIC)

`ContractBody::TOPIC`[- so an unchanged contract stays wire-identical while the compile-time](https://docs.rs/y2026_1/enum.Api.html)

`Api``Api` bound stays
distinct. See [for the inheritance and shape-identity rules. A not-yet-promoted generation is authored as](https://docs.rs/phoxal-macros/0.19.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_macros/macro.phoxal_api_tree.html)

`phoxal_api_tree!``preview version y2026_N extends ...`; it still lives at the final module path
(`phoxal_api::y2026_N`) but is available only when the matching
`preview-y2026_N` Cargo feature is enabled. The generated module docs call out
the preview status, and [records the lifecycle without changing schema ids, topics, or wire bytes.](https://docs.rs/trait.ApiVersion.html#associatedconstant.IS_PREVIEW)

`ApiVersion::IS_PREVIEW`[§](https://docs.rs#one-api-version-per-participant-per-contract-compatibility-per-graph)One API version per participant; per-contract compatibility per graph

A participant authors against exactly one version module
(`use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`) and declares it on the derive
(`#[phoxal(api = y2026_1)]`). Every handle body is bound
`ContractBody<Api = R::Api>`, so passing a body from another API version is a
compile error (D60). Across the graph, participants may mix generations:
compatibility is proven per contract by `schema_id` agreement (#16) - a
contract whose transitive wire shape is unchanged hashes identically across
generations, so its users keep interoperating.

[§](https://docs.rs#plain-serde-wire-bodies-schema-in-metadata)Plain serde wire bodies, schema in metadata

A wire body is just its serde encoding - there is no `{"v":…}` envelope or any
other version tag inside the payload (D62). The four pieces of routing
identity travel as bus metadata alongside the encoded body, not in it:

- the **schema id**(`ContractBody::SCHEMA_ID`
- the **version**(`ApiVersion::ID``"y2026_1"`), informational,
- the **family**(`ContractBody::FAMILY``"drive::State"`),
- the **codec**that produced the bytes.

Keeping these out of the payload means the body bytes for an unchanged contract are identical across versions and codecs; the envelope/metadata layer owns schema id, version, and family.

[§](https://docs.rs#family-and-topic)Family and topic

Both identifiers are derived from the contract node’s path in the tree, never written by hand:

- `ContractBody::FAMILY`- `::`-joined node path plus the body type name, e.g.- `component::motor::Command`. It excludes dynamic variables, so every instance of a per-instance node shares one family.
- `ContractBody::TOPIC`- `/`-joined key with each dynamic node contributing a- `{var}`placeholder, e.g.- `component/{instance}/motor/{capability}/command`. A fully static path has a literal key (- `drive/state`).

[§](https://docs.rs#the-api-local-topic-builder)The api-local topic builder

Each version module exposes a `topic` builder that mirrors the node tree:
`api::topic::new()` returns a root, one method per top-level node walks down the
tree, a dynamic node’s method takes its variable as `impl Display`, and a leaf
method binds the topic’s side-branded kind to its version-local body. For
example `api::topic::new().drive().state()` yields a
`Topic<Subscribe<drive::State>>` (the CLIENT observes the owner’s `state`) over
the static key `drive/state`, and
`api::topic::new().component("base").motor("left").command()` fills the dynamic
segments to produce `component/base/motor/left/command`. Because the builder is
generated from the same tree as `FAMILY`/`TOPIC`, the built key and the
documented key stay in lockstep.

[§](https://docs.rs#owner-side-topicinternal)Owner side: `topic::internal`

The PUBLIC `topic::new()...` chain above is the **client** side. The matching
**owner** side lives at `api::topic::internal::new(cap)...` (L1 + L2, plan #00):
the same node tree and keys, but the leaf brands flip so the owner gets the side
it must take - `api::topic::internal::new(cap).drive().state()` is
`Topic<Publish<drive::State>>` (the owner publishes its telemetry), and
`api::topic::internal::new(cap).drive().target()` is `Topic<Subscribe<drive::Target>>`
(the owner reads its command input). A query owner reaches its `ServeQuery`
brand the same way. The `internal` chain is the deliberate, greppable owner
opt-in; a participant acquires the topics of its OWN node through it and everything
it consumes through the public chain.

The `internal::new` entry requires the runner-minted owner capability
([ OwnerCap](https://docs.rs/phoxal-bus/0.20.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_bus/capability/struct.OwnerCap.html), Layer 2): a participant obtains it from

`phoxal::SetupContext::owner_capability()` and passes it in. On the documented
surface, owning a topic therefore cannot happen by accident - only with a
capability the runner mints.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [y2026_1](https://docs.rs/y2026_1/index.html)
- Dated API version `y2026_1`- version-local wire bodies + topics.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [ApiVersion](https://docs.rs/trait.ApiVersion.html)
- The contract primitive traits, re-exported from the `phoxal-bus`crate (the ABI floor) so they stay addressable at`phoxal_api::ApiVersion`/`phoxal_api::ContractBody`.
- [Contract](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html)- Body
- The contract primitive traits, re-exported from the `phoxal-bus`crate (the ABI floor) so they stay addressable at`phoxal_api::ApiVersion`/`phoxal_api::ContractBody`.

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-api/0.19.3/src/phoxal_api/lib.rs.html

# phoxal_api/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! The single API layer (D60/D61).
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! This crate is the dated API contract tree. It depends only on the
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! [`phoxal-bus`](phoxal_bus) ABI floor (the contract primitive traits and the
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! typed-topic builders) and the [`phoxal-macros`](phoxal_macros) proc-macros; it
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! does **not** depend on the `phoxal` engine. A participant depends on both crates
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! and imports the API tree directly with `use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`, so
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! `phoxal_api::y2026_1`, `phoxal_api::ApiVersion`, and `phoxal_api::ContractBody`
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! are the canonical paths.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! # Dated API versions
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! An API version is a **dated module** (`phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …) generated by
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! [`phoxal_api_tree!`]. Each version module carries:
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! - a zero-variant marker `enum Api {}` implementing [`ApiVersion`], whose
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!   [`ApiVersion::ID`] is the dated module name (`"y2026_1"`);
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! - the version-local wire bodies, one `pub mod` per contract node holding plain
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!   serde structs/enums and their [`ContractBody`] impls;
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! - an api-local `topic` builder rooted at `topic::new()`.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! Versions can build on earlier ones with `version y2026_2 extends y2026_1`:
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! every inherited node and type is re-emitted *fresh* under the new module - same
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! [`ContractBody::FAMILY`] and [`ContractBody::TOPIC`], a different [`Api`] - so an
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! unchanged contract stays wire-identical while the compile-time `Api` bound stays
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! distinct. See [`phoxal_api_tree!`] for the inheritance and shape-identity rules.
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! A not-yet-promoted generation is authored as
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! `preview version y2026_N extends ...`; it still lives at the final module path
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! (`phoxal_api::y2026_N`) but is available only when the matching
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! `preview-y2026_N` Cargo feature is enabled. The generated module docs call out
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! the preview status, and [`ApiVersion::IS_PREVIEW`] records the lifecycle without
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! changing schema ids, topics, or wire bytes.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! [`Api`]: y2026_1::Api
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! # One API version per participant; per-contract compatibility per graph
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! A participant authors against exactly one version module
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! (`use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`) and declares it on the derive
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! (`#[phoxal(api = y2026_1)]`). Every handle body is bound
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! `ContractBody<Api = R::Api>`, so passing a body from another API version is a
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! compile error (D60). Across the graph, participants may mix generations:
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! compatibility is proven per contract by `schema_id` agreement (#16) - a
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! contract whose transitive wire shape is unchanged hashes identically across
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! generations, so its users keep interoperating.
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! # Plain serde wire bodies, schema in metadata
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! A wire body is just its serde encoding - there is no `{"v":…}` envelope or any
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! other version tag inside the payload (D62). The four pieces of routing
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! identity travel as bus metadata alongside the encoded body, not in it:
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! - the **schema id** ([`ContractBody::SCHEMA_ID`]), the compatibility key,
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! - the **version** ([`ApiVersion::ID`], e.g. `"y2026_1"`), informational,
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! - the **family** ([`ContractBody::FAMILY`], e.g. `"drive::State"`),
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! - the **codec** that produced the bytes.
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! Keeping these out of the payload means the body bytes for an unchanged contract
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! are identical across versions and codecs; the envelope/metadata layer owns
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! schema id, version, and family.
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! # Family and topic
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! Both identifiers are derived from the contract node's path in the tree, never
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! written by hand:
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! - [`ContractBody::FAMILY`] is the `::`-joined node path plus the body type name,
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!   e.g. `component::motor::Command`. It excludes dynamic variables, so every
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!   instance of a per-instance node shares one family.
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! - [`ContractBody::TOPIC`] is the versionless `/`-joined key with each dynamic
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!   node contributing a `{var}` placeholder, e.g.
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!   `component/{instance}/motor/{capability}/command`. A fully static path has a
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!   literal key (`drive/state`).
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! # The api-local topic builder
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! Each version module exposes a `topic` builder that mirrors the node tree:
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! `api::topic::new()` returns a root, one method per top-level node walks down the
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! tree, a dynamic node's method takes its variable as `impl Display`, and a leaf
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! method binds the topic's side-branded kind to its version-local body. For
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! example `api::topic::new().drive().state()` yields a
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! `Topic<Subscribe<drive::State>>` (the CLIENT observes the owner's `state`) over
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! the static key `drive/state`, and
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! `api::topic::new().component("base").motor("left").command()` fills the dynamic
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! segments to produce `component/base/motor/left/command`. Because the builder is
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! generated from the same tree as `FAMILY`/`TOPIC`, the built key and the
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! documented key stay in lockstep.
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//!
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! ## Owner side: `topic::internal`
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! The PUBLIC `topic::new()...` chain above is the **client** side. The matching
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! **owner** side lives at `api::topic::internal::new(cap)...` (L1 + L2, plan #00):
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! the same node tree and keys, but the leaf brands flip so the owner gets the side
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! it must take - `api::topic::internal::new(cap).drive().state()` is
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! `Topic<Publish<drive::State>>` (the owner publishes its telemetry), and
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! `api::topic::internal::new(cap).drive().target()` is `Topic<Subscribe<drive::Target>>`
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! (the owner reads its command input). A query owner reaches its `ServeQuery`
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! brand the same way. The `internal` chain is the deliberate, greppable owner
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! opt-in; a participant acquires the topics of its OWN node through it and everything
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! it consumes through the public chain.
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! The `internal::new` entry requires the runner-minted owner capability
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! ([`OwnerCap`](phoxal_bus::OwnerCap), Layer 2): a participant obtains it from
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! `phoxal::SetupContext::owner_capability()` and passes it in. On the documented
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! surface, owning a topic therefore cannot happen by accident - only with a
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! capability the runner mints.
[107](https://docs.rs#107)
[108](https://docs.rs#108)use phoxal_macros::phoxal_api_tree;
[109](https://docs.rs#109)
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// The contract primitive traits, re-exported from the `phoxal-bus` crate (the
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// ABI floor) so they stay addressable at `phoxal_api::ApiVersion` /
[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// `phoxal_api::ContractBody`.
[113](https://docs.rs#113)///
[114](https://docs.rs#114)/// - [`ApiVersion`] is the marker trait identifying one dated API version (D60),
[115](https://docs.rs#115)///   implemented only by the zero-variant `enum Api {}` that [`phoxal_api_tree!`]
[116](https://docs.rs#116)///   generates inside each version module; its `ID` is the dated module name
[117](https://docs.rs#117)///   (`"y2026_1"`) and is carried in bus metadata as informational provenance.
[118](https://docs.rs#118)///   Its `IS_PREVIEW` const is lifecycle metadata only.
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// - [`ContractBody`] is a version-local wire body (D61): a plain serde type
[120](https://docs.rs#120)///   bound to exactly one [`ApiVersion`] and one contract family/topic. Every
[121](https://docs.rs#121)///   body declared inside a [`phoxal_api_tree!`] node gets a generated impl;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)///   handles, `SetupContext` builders, and the `Service`/`Driver` derive
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///   assertions key off its `Api`/`FAMILY`/`SCHEMA_ID`/`TOPIC`. Runtime decode
[124](https://docs.rs#124)///   compatibility keys off `SCHEMA_ID`; its serde encoding *is* the wire payload,
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///   with no version envelope (D62).
[126](https://docs.rs#126)pub use phoxal_bus::{ApiVersion, ContractBody};
[127](https://docs.rs#127)
[128](https://docs.rs#128)phoxal_api_tree! {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    version y2026_1 {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)        drive {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)            /// Why actuation authority is in its current state.
[132](https://docs.rs#132)            enum StopReason {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)                NoTarget,
[134](https://docs.rs#134)                EmergencyStop,
[135](https://docs.rs#135)                Fault,
[136](https://docs.rs#136)            }
[137](https://docs.rs#137)
[138](https://docs.rs#138)            /// Whether the drive is actively commanding the actuators.
[139](https://docs.rs#139)            enum ActuatorAuthority {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)                Active,
[141](https://docs.rs#141)                Stopped,
[142](https://docs.rs#142)            }
[143](https://docs.rs#143)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            /// A requested or limited planar velocity.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            struct Target {
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                linear_x_mps: f32,
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                angular_z_radps: f32,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)                curvature_limit_radpm: Option<f32>,
[149](https://docs.rs#149)            }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)
[151](https://docs.rs#151)            /// The drive participant's published control state.
[152](https://docs.rs#152)            struct State {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)                target: Target,
[154](https://docs.rs#154)                limited_target: Target,
[155](https://docs.rs#155)                actuator_authority: ActuatorAuthority,
[156](https://docs.rs#156)                stop_reason: Option<StopReason>,
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            }
[158](https://docs.rs#158)
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            topic target: command Target;
[160](https://docs.rs#160)            topic state: state State;
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        }
[162](https://docs.rs#162)
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        battery {
[164](https://docs.rs#164)            /// Battery state - a family that exists only from y2026_1 on.
[165](https://docs.rs#165)            struct State {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)                voltage_v: f32,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)                current_a: f32,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)                charge_ratio: f32,
[169](https://docs.rs#169)            }
[170](https://docs.rs#170)

[172](https://docs.rs#172)        }
[173](https://docs.rs#173)
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        safety {
[175](https://docs.rs#175)            /// Safety participant decision for a candidate motion command.
[176](https://docs.rs#176)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            enum SafetyDecision {
[178](https://docs.rs#178)                Allow,
[179](https://docs.rs#179)                Slow,
[180](https://docs.rs#180)                Stop,
[181](https://docs.rs#181)                EmergencyStop,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)                UnknownConservative,
[183](https://docs.rs#183)            }
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)            /// An inclusive `[min, max]` bound on a scalar control axis.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)            struct Constraint {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)                min: f64,
[188](https://docs.rs#188)                max: f64,
[189](https://docs.rs#189)            }
[190](https://docs.rs#190)
[191](https://docs.rs#191)            /// Per-axis velocity bounds the safety participant will allow.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)            struct MotionConstraint {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)                linear_x_mps: Constraint,
[194](https://docs.rs#194)                angular_z_radps: Constraint,
[195](https://docs.rs#195)            }
[196](https://docs.rs#196)
[197](https://docs.rs#197)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[198](https://docs.rs#198)            #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
[199](https://docs.rs#199)            enum SafetyReasonCode {
[200](https://docs.rs#200)                ObstacleDetected,
[201](https://docs.rs#201)                BatteryLow,
[202](https://docs.rs#202)                BatteryCritical,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)                DriveFault,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)                LocalizationLost,
[205](https://docs.rs#205)                SourceStale,
[206](https://docs.rs#206)                EmergencyStopEngaged,
[207](https://docs.rs#207)                Unknown,
[208](https://docs.rs#208)            }
[209](https://docs.rs#209)
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            /// A coded reason behind a safety decision, with optional detail text.
[211](https://docs.rs#211)            struct SafetyReason {
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                code: SafetyReasonCode,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)                detail: Option<String>,
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            }
[215](https://docs.rs#215)
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            /// Revisions of the inputs a safety decision was computed against.
[217](https://docs.rs#217)            struct SafetySourceRevision {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)                localization: Option<u64>,
[219](https://docs.rs#219)                map: Option<u64>,
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            }
[221](https://docs.rs#221)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            /// The safety participant's authorization for downstream motion: the
[223](https://docs.rs#223)            /// decision, the motion it approves, why, and when it expires.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            struct SafetyAuthorization {
[225](https://docs.rs#225)                decision: SafetyDecision,
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                approved_motion: MotionConstraint,
[227](https://docs.rs#227)                reasons: Vec<SafetyReason>,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                source_revision: SafetySourceRevision,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                expires_at_ns: Option<u64>,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)            }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)            /// The safety participant's published status: current decision + reasons.
[233](https://docs.rs#233)            struct Status {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)                decision: SafetyDecision,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)                active_reasons: Vec<SafetyReason>,
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            }
[237](https://docs.rs#237)
[238](https://docs.rs#238)            /// A request to engage or release the emergency stop.
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            #[derive(Eq)]
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            struct EmergencyStopRequest {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)                engaged: bool,
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            }
[243](https://docs.rs#243)
[244](https://docs.rs#244)            topic authorization: state SafetyAuthorization;
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            topic state: state Status;
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            topic estop: command EmergencyStopRequest;
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        }

[249](https://docs.rs#249)        mission {

[253](https://docs.rs#253)                y_m: f64,

[261](https://docs.rs#261)                Resume,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                Cancel,

[264](https://docs.rs#264)

[273](https://docs.rs#273)            }
[274](https://docs.rs#274)

[279](https://docs.rs#279)                detail: Option<String>,
[280](https://docs.rs#280)            }

[299](https://docs.rs#299)        frame {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            /// A parent → child rigid transform (translation + xyzw quaternion).
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            struct FrameTransform {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)                parent_frame_id: String,
[303](https://docs.rs#303)                child_frame_id: String,
[304](https://docs.rs#304)                translation_m: [f64; 3],
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                rotation_quat_xyzw: [f64; 4],
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                stamp_ns: Option<u64>,
[307](https://docs.rs#307)            }
[308](https://docs.rs#308)
[309](https://docs.rs#309)            /// Transforms that do not change over time.
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            struct StaticTransforms {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                transforms: Vec<FrameTransform>,
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            /// The current transform tree.
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            struct Tree {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)                transforms: Vec<FrameTransform>,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)            }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)
[319](https://docs.rs#319)            /// Ask for the transform between two frames, optionally at a time.
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            struct LookupRequest {
[321](https://docs.rs#321)                target_frame_id: String,
[322](https://docs.rs#322)                source_frame_id: String,
[323](https://docs.rs#323)                at_ns: Option<u64>,
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            }
[325](https://docs.rs#325)
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            /// The resolved transform, or `None` if it is not available.
[327](https://docs.rs#327)            struct LookupResponse {
[328](https://docs.rs#328)                transform: Option<FrameTransform>,
[329](https://docs.rs#329)            }
[330](https://docs.rs#330)
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            topic tree: state Tree;
[332](https://docs.rs#332)            topic static_transforms: state StaticTransforms;
[333](https://docs.rs#333)            topic lookup: query LookupRequest => LookupResponse;
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        }
[335](https://docs.rs#335)
[336](https://docs.rs#336)        power {
[337](https://docs.rs#337)            /// A platform power command.
[338](https://docs.rs#338)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[339](https://docs.rs#339)            enum Command {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                Reboot,
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                Shutdown,
[342](https://docs.rs#342)            }
[343](https://docs.rs#343)
[344](https://docs.rs#344)            /// Where the power participant is in handling a command.
[345](https://docs.rs#345)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[346](https://docs.rs#346)            enum Status {
[347](https://docs.rs#347)                Idle,
[348](https://docs.rs#348)                Rebooting,
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                ShuttingDown,
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                Failed,
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            }
[352](https://docs.rs#352)
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            /// Why a power command was rejected outright.
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[355](https://docs.rs#355)            #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            enum RejectedReason {
[357](https://docs.rs#357)                SupervisorUnavailable,
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                SupervisorReturnedHttp,
[359](https://docs.rs#359)            }
[360](https://docs.rs#360)
[361](https://docs.rs#361)            /// Why an accepted power command later failed.
[362](https://docs.rs#362)            #[derive(Copy, Eq)]
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
[364](https://docs.rs#364)            enum FailedReason {
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                SupervisorTransport,
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            }

[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        // Per-instance component capabilities (D17/D38: framework participant / driver
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        // territory). `component(instance)` selects a manifest-declared component;
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        // each child `kind(capability)` is a self-contained node whose key is
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        // `component/{instance}/<kind>/{capability}/<leaf>`. Nodes duplicate any
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        // types they share by design - the node path disambiguates, so the names
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        // are path-local.
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        component(instance) {
[631](https://docs.rs#631)            motor(capability) {

[635](https://docs.rs#635)                    Torque(f32),
[636](https://docs.rs#636)                    Stop,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)                }
[638](https://docs.rs#638)
[639](https://docs.rs#639)                topic command: command Command;
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            }

# phoxal_bus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-bus/0.20.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_bus/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#phoxal-bus)phoxal-bus

The Phoxal bus ABI floor: the Zenoh-native `bus_abi` boundary (D26/D62) plus
the two contract primitive traits ([ ApiVersion](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ApiVersion.html) /

[) the bus client is generic over.](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ContractBody.html)

`ContractBody`Samples are Zenoh-native: the key (`<namespace>/robots/<robot-id>/<topic>`),
an encoding string + a [ BusMetadata](https://docs.rs/metadata/struct.BusMetadata.html) attachment (schema id, family, codec,
api version, and provenance), and a plain MessagePack body payload - there is no Phoxal frame
independent of Zenoh, and no

`{"v":…}` version tag in the body (D62).The concrete dated API versions (`y2026_1`, …) generated by the
`phoxal_api_tree!` macro - and their [ ApiVersion](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ApiVersion.html) /

[impls - live in the](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ContractBody.html)

`ContractBody``phoxal-api` crate (`phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …), which also re-exports
these two traits. The `phoxal` engine re-exports the typed authoring subset at
`phoxal::bus`, so the traits are also reachable as `phoxal::bus::ApiVersion` /
`phoxal::bus::ContractBody`. The raw session-opening surface lives behind the
explicit `phoxal::raw` opt-in.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use abi::`- [BUS_ABI](https://docs.rs/abi/constant.BUS_ABI.html);
- `pub use abi::`- [BusAbi](https://docs.rs/abi/struct.BusAbi.html);
- `pub use abi::`- [CodecId](https://docs.rs/abi/enum.CodecId.html);
- `pub use abi::`- [encoding_string](https://docs.rs/abi/fn.encoding_string.html);
- `pub use capability::`- [OwnerCap](https://docs.rs/capability/struct.OwnerCap.html);
- `pub use codec::`- [Codec](https://docs.rs/codec/trait.Codec.html);
- `pub use codec::`- [CodecError](https://docs.rs/codec/enum.CodecError.html);
- `pub use codec::`- [MessagePack](https://docs.rs/codec/struct.MessagePack.html);
- `pub use contract::`- [ApiVersion](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ApiVersion.html);
- `pub use contract::`- [ContractBody](https://docs.rs/contract/trait.ContractBody.html);
- `pub use contract::`- [TopicRole](https://docs.rs/contract/enum.TopicRole.html);
- `pub use error::`- [BusError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.BusError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [abi](https://docs.rs/abi/index.html)
- `bus_abi`- the framework-owned wire envelope (D26/D45/D62).
- [capability](https://docs.rs/capability/index.html)
- The plan #00 Layer 2 owner capability.
- [codec](https://docs.rs/codec/index.html)
- The body codec boundary (D62). One codec in v1: MessagePack with named fields.
- [contract](https://docs.rs/contract/index.html)
- The contract primitive traits (D60/D61): the API-version marker and the version-local wire body.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Bus error type.
- [handle](https://docs.rs/handle/index.html)
- Body-typed handles over the `bus_abi`boundary (D35).
- [metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata/index.html)
- `BusMetadata`- the per-sample attachment (D43c/D62).
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- Query error wire shape (D31/D43f).
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- Server-side query handling: a thin wrapper over a Zenoh queryable that the
runner uses to drive `#[server]`/`#[server_snapshot]`handlers (D16/D31).
- [session](https://docs.rs/session/index.html)
- The Zenoh session wrapper: key root, namespace validation, the non-blocking outbound queue (D43e), and health counters.
- [topic](https://docs.rs/topic/index.html)
- Typed topics - the api-local builder output (D61), side-branded for L1 (plan #00).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Logical](https://docs.rs/struct.LogicalTime.html)- Time
- Logical robot time: an epoch + a nanosecond timestamp in the clock’s domain.

# phoxal_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-macros/0.19.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_macros/index.html

## Expand description

Proc-macros for the phoxal framework.

Three macro families make up the authoring surface:

- `phoxal_api_tree!`- `phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …), their version-local body types, the- `ContractBody`/- `ApiVersion`impls, and the api-local topic builders.
- `Service`- `Driver`- `Tool`- `Simulator`- `#[phoxal(id = …, api = …, config = …, contracts(…))]`attribute and emits the static metadata (- `ParticipantSpec`) the runner and- `emit-apis`consume.
- `behavior`- `#[phoxal::behavior]`attribute on the inherent impl; it reads- `#[setup]`/- `#[step(hz = N)]`/- `#[shutdown]`plus the query-side- `#[server]`/- `#[server_snapshot]`/- `#[snapshot]`and emits the lifecycle and server dispatch (- `ParticipantBehavior`).

The struct/impl macros are paired: the derive selects the API version, records
the artifact kind, and contributes the field-derived contracts, while
`#[phoxal::behavior]` adds the lifecycle methods and the server-side contracts.
Both reference the one API version chosen by the derive, and the generated
`ContractBody<Api = Self::Api>` assertions make a body from a different
version a compile error.

The participant authoring macros (`derive@Service` / `derive@Driver` /
`derive@Tool` / `derive@Simulator` / `macro@behavior`) reference the framework
through `::phoxal::…`; the engine crate makes that path resolve to itself with
`extern crate self as phoxal;`. The
`phoxal_api_tree!` output instead targets the bus ABI floor directly as
`::phoxal_bus`, since it is invoked in the `phoxal-api` crate, which does not
depend on the engine.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [phoxal_](https://docs.rs/macro.phoxal_api_tree.html)- api_ - tree
- Declare a dated API-version tree of version-local wire bodies + topics.

# phoxal_api_tree in phoxal_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-macros/0.19.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_macros/macro.phoxal_api_tree.html

`phoxal_api_tree!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

Declare a dated API-version tree of version-local wire bodies + topics.

One invocation owns one or more `version y2026_N { … }` blocks; each becomes a
`pub mod y2026_N` under wherever the macro is invoked. A generation may be
authored as `preview version y2026_N`; it is still emitted at `y2026_N`, but
behind the per-generation Cargo feature `preview-y2026_N` and with
`ApiVersion::IS_PREVIEW = true`. In this workspace it is invoked in the
`phoxal-api` crate (the canonical import is
`use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`), and the generated tree references the bus
ABI floor as `::phoxal_bus`. A
`version y2026_N extends y2026_M { … }` inherits the
earlier version’s effective tree (the parent must be declared earlier in the
same invocation); see the `api_tree` module docs for the inheritance rules.

[§](https://docs.rs#node-grammar)Node grammar

A version body is a tree of **nodes**. A node is either static (`name { … }`)
or dynamic (`name(var) { … }`, binding exactly one variable), and may nest to
any depth. Inside a node block, in any order:

- `struct …`/- `enum …`- a version-local wire body. Macro-declared structs get public fields; every body gets the standard derive set (- `Clone`,- `Debug`,- `PartialEq`,- `serde::Serialize`/- `Deserialize`).
- `topic <leaf>: command <Body>;`- a pub/sub topic the owning service subscribes (a control input).
- `topic <leaf>: state <Body>;`- a pub/sub topic the owning service publishes (telemetry/output). Same wire shape as- `command`, but the side-branded builders give it the inverse brand (see- *Generated topic builders*below).
- `topic <leaf>: query <Req> => <Resp>;`- a request/response topic.
- a child node (`name { … }`/`name(var) { … }`).

Doc-comments and attributes attach to the next `struct`/`enum`; `topic`
declarations and child nodes take none.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-each-topic-derives-from-its-node-path)What each topic derives from its node path

A topic carries no per-topic params; its identity is derived from the path of nodes enclosing it:

- **key**- the- `/`-joined node segments plus the leaf, where a static node contributes- `name`and a dynamic node contributes- `name/{var}`(e.g.- `component/{instance}/motor/{capability}/command`).
- `FAMILY`- `::`-joined node names plus the body type, with the- `(var)`parts excluded (e.g.- `component::motor::Command`).
- **body type path**-- `phoxal_api::y2026_N::<node>::…::<Body>`; variables never appear in the module path.

A topic is dynamic when its node path contains at least one `(var)` node, and
static otherwise.

[§](https://docs.rs#generated-topic-builders)Generated topic builders

Each version also gets an api-local `topic` module emitted with BOTH side trees
(L1, plan #00). `topic::new()` returns a `Root` for the PUBLIC **client** side;
`topic::internal::new(cap)` returns a `Root` for the OWNER side (a deliberate,
greppable owner opt-in). The owner entry requires the runner-minted
`phoxal_bus::OwnerCap` (L2): a participant passes `ctx.owner_capability()`. Both
have a method per node that walks the identical
tree (a dynamic node’s method takes its variable as `impl Display`) and a leaf
method that returns a typed `bus::Topic<Kind>` with the key formatted from the
carried variables. The leaf brand is side-specific: on the client side a
`command` leaf is `Publish<Body>`, a `state` leaf is `Subscribe<Body>`, and a
`query` leaf is `AskQuery<Req, Resp>`; on the owner side those flip to
`Subscribe<Body>` / `Publish<Body>` / `ServeQuery<Req, Resp>`.

---

# ContractBody in phoxal_api - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-api/0.19.3/phoxal_api/trait.ContractBody.html

```
pub trait ContractBody:

```
[Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html)
    + [DeserializeOwned](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.DeserializeOwned.html)
    + [Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html)
    + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)
    + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)
    + 'static {
    type [Api](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Api): [ApiVersion](https://docs.rs/trait.ApiVersion.html);
    const [FAMILY](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.FAMILY): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html);
    const [SCHEMA_ID](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.SCHEMA_ID): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html);
    const [TOPIC](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.TOPIC): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html);
}## Expand description

The contract primitive traits, re-exported from the `phoxal-bus` crate (the
ABI floor) so they stay addressable at `phoxal_api::ApiVersion` /
`phoxal_api::ContractBody`.

- `ApiVersion`- `enum Api {}`that- `phoxal_api_tree!`- `ID`is the dated module name (- `"y2026_1"`) and is carried in bus metadata as informational provenance. Its- `IS_PREVIEW`const is lifecycle metadata only.
- `ContractBody`- `ApiVersion`- `phoxal_api_tree!`- `SetupContext`builders, and the- `Service`/- `Driver`derive assertions key off its- `Api`/- `FAMILY`/- `SCHEMA_ID`/- `TOPIC`. Runtime decode compatibility keys off- `SCHEMA_ID`; its serde encoding- *is*the wire payload, with no version envelope (D62). A version-local wire body: a plain serde type bound to exactly one- `ApiVersion`

Every body declared inside a `phoxal_api_tree!` node gets a generated impl.
Handles, `SetupContext` builders, and the `Service`/`Driver` derive assertions
all key off [ Api](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedtype.Api)/

[/](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.FAMILY)

`FAMILY`[, which is how a body from the wrong API version is rejected at compile time.](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.TOPIC)

`TOPIC`The serde encoding of an implementor *is* the wire payload; there is no version
envelope (D62). Version and family travel as bus metadata, derived from
[ Api](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedtype.Api) and

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.FAMILY)

`FAMILY`Runtime decode compatibility keys off [ SCHEMA_ID](https://docs.rs/trait.ContractBody.html#associatedconstant.SCHEMA_ID),
not the graph API version.

`SCHEMA_ID` is a normalized hash of the body’s
transitive wire shape. The canonical hash input is `phoxal.schema/v0\n`
followed by this grammar:```
body    = unit | newtype | tuple | struct | enum
struct  = "struct{" field* "}"
field   = "f" byte_len ":" utf8_name "=" ty ";"
enum    = "enum(" repr "){" variant* "}"
repr    = "external" | "internal(tag=" name ")"
        | "adjacent(tag=" name ",content=" name ")" | "untagged"
variant = "v" byte_len ":" utf8_name "=" payload ";"
payload = unit | "newtype(" ty ")" | tuple | struct
newtype = "newtype(" ty ")"
tuple   = "tuple(" (ty ";")* ")"
ty      = nil | bool | string | bytes | integer | float | option | seq | array
        | map | tuple | body
integer = "u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "u64" | "u128"
        | "i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "i64" | "i128"
float   = "f32" | "f64"
option  = "option(" ty ")"
seq     = "seq(" ty ")"
array   = "array[" decimal_len "](" ty ")"
map     = "map(" ty "," ty ")"
name    = byte_len ":" utf8_name
```
Fields stay in declared order and use their serde wire names, including
`rename` and `rename_all`. Enums include serde representation mode, variant
wire names, and payload shapes. Nested API-tree structs and enums are expanded
transitively, with generic type parameters substituted by concrete type
arguments before expansion. Only understood serde attributes and known
wire-neutral attributes such as doc comments and simple derives are accepted.
Non-wire details such as Rust type identifiers when the wire shape has already
been expanded are excluded. The displayed id is lower-hex
`sha256(canonical_string)`, truncated to the first 16 hex characters.

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

Canonical contract family id: the `::`-joined node path plus the body type
name, with dynamic variables excluded, e.g. `"drive::State"` or
`"component::motor::Command"`.

Per-contract compatibility id: lower-hex SHA-256 of the canonical transitive wire-shape string, truncated to 16 hex characters.

Versionless topic key: the `/`-joined node path plus the topic leaf, with
each dynamic node contributing a `{var}` placeholder, e.g. `"drive/state"`
or `"component/{instance}/motor/{capability}/command"`. The concrete key is
produced by the api-local `topic` builder, which fills the placeholders.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# OwnerCap in phoxal_bus::capability - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/phoxal-bus/0.20.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/phoxal_bus/capability/struct.OwnerCap.html

`pub struct OwnerCap(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The plan #00 Layer 2 owner capability: a runner-minted token required to construct the OWNER side of a topic on the documented authoring surface.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-it-is-for)What it is for

Layer 1 (side branding) makes taking the *wrong side* of a topic a compile
error, but on its own it left the owner side reachable through the owner
builder with no proof of authority. Layer 2 closes the “any participant can
mint itself the owner side” hole: the owner builder entry
`api::topic::internal::new(cap)` now *requires* an `OwnerCap`, and the ONLY
documented way to obtain one is
[ phoxal::SetupContext::owner_capability()](https://docs.rs/phoxal). The runner mints the single

`OwnerCap` it hands to `SetupContext` before `#[setup]` runs, so a participant opts
into owning its own topics deliberately and visibly:[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let cap = ctx.owner_capability();
let pub_ = ctx.publisher(api::topic::internal::new(cap).drive().state()).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#honest-residual-not-a-hard-guarantee)Honest residual (not a hard guarantee)

This is a “not-by-accident / not-on-the-documented-surface” gate, not a hard
guarantee (plan #00 lines 129-131). The raw `#[doc(hidden)]` [ Topic](https://docs.rs/topic/struct.Topic.html)
constructors (

`Topic::new_static` / `Topic::new_owned`) are still `pub`, so a
determined caller can forge an owner-branded topic by hand without ever
obtaining an `OwnerCap`. Those constructors must stay `pub` because the
proc-macro-generated `phoxal_api_tree!` code in the separate `phoxal-api` crate
has to call them across the crate boundary, and a `pub(crate)` constructor
cannot cross it. Layer 2 therefore raises the bar on the documented surface (no
owner topic is built by accident) without claiming to seal the escape hatch.## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

# pseudoroot

A Rust implementation of fakeroot using library interposition
(`LD_PRELOAD` on Linux, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` on macOS). Commands run as
if they had root privileges without requiring real root access.

## Quick start

```
# Implicit run (fakeroot-style)
# Explicit subcommand form (equivalent)
```
`pdr` is a single self-contained binary — the interposed library is embedded
at build time and extracted to a cache directory on first use, so no
`libpseudoroot_lib.so`/`.dylib` needs to exist anywhere on disk beforehand.
`pdr start` runs the optional persistent daemon in-process, so no separate
`pdrd` binary is needed for that either; a standalone `pdrd` is still
available (see [Build and test](https://docs.rs#build-and-test)) as a dedicated daemon
process for external orchestration.

## CLI options

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--uid <UID>` | Fake UID | 0 |
| `--gid <GID>` | Fake GID | 0 |
| `--daemon` | Attach to an existing `pdrd`instead of a per-invocation session | off |
| `--socket-path <PATH>` | Daemon socket path | `/tmp/pseudoroot.sock` |
| `start`/`stop`/`status` | Manage the daemon | — |
| `print-library-path` | Print the interposed library path | — |
| `start --verbose` | Enable verbose daemon logging | off |
| `start --cleanup` | Clean up socket file on daemon exit | off |

By default each invocation gets its own session, shared across `exec`
within it. To share state across separate invocations, use a daemon:

```
```
## Rust API (fakeroost-compatible)

Swap backends by changing the import only:

```
use FakerootCommandExt;
```
## Environment variables

- `PSEUDOROOT_UID`/- `PSEUDOROOT_GID`— fake uid/gid (default: 0)
- `PSEUDOROOT_DAEMON_SOCKET`— attach to an existing daemon (skips session auto-start)
- `PSEUDOROOT_STANDALONE`— per-process state only (no session)
- `PSEUDOROOT_SESSION_SHM`— set to- `0`to use an in-process daemon thread instead of the shared-memory map for session mode
- `PSEUDOROOT_LIB`— override the interposed library path, bypassing the embedded copy entirely (tests, custom installs, debugging a locally built- `pseudoroot-lib`)

## Documentation

- [Architecture](https://docs.rs/docs/architecture.md)— crate layout, inode-keyed state model, platform support, interposed syscall families.
- [Benchmarks](https://docs.rs/docs/benchmarks.md)— comparison against native,- `fakeroot`, and- `fakeroost`; on a 128-core Linux machine pseudoroot sustains ~7.4M faked- `stat()`calls/sec vs fakeroot's ~44.5K, and on a MacBook Pro with M2 Max (12-core ARM64) ~899K calls/sec vs fakeroot's ~43K.

## Comparison

| Feature | pseudoroot | fakeroot | fakeroost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | `LD_PRELOAD` | `LD_PRELOAD` | ptrace supervisor |
| Platforms | Linux, macOS | Linux | Linux |
| xattr / setcap | Faked | Faked | Faked |
| mknod unprivileged | Placeholder + fake metadata | Yes | Yes |
| Multi-process state | SHM session or daemon ( `pdrd`) | `faked` | N/A (single run) |
| Rust API | `FakerootCommandExt` | C only | `FakerootCommandExt` |

## Build and test

```
```
`pdr` embeds the interposed library at build time: `pseudoroot/build.rs`
compiles the cdylib from the source bundled at `pseudoroot/interpose/` and
`include_bytes!`es it into the binary — so `cargo install pseudoroot` from
crates.io is self-contained, with no separate `.so`/`.dylib` to install.
For a standalone `pdrd` daemon binary, build the `pseudoroot-daemon` package
directly: `cargo build -p pseudoroot-daemon`.

## License

Licensed under [MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT).

## Contributing

See [AGENTS.md](https://docs.rs/AGENTS.md) for conventions (Conventional Commits, style,
MSRV checks).

Luca Barbato [lu_zero@gentoo.org](mailto:lu_zero@gentoo.org)

# ctor 0.2.9 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ctor/^0.2

# rust-ctor

Module initialization/teardown functions for Rust (like `__attribute__((constructor))` in C/C++) for Linux, OSX, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Illumos, OpenBSD, DragonFlyBSD, Android, iOS, and Windows.

This library currently requires **Rust > 1.31.0** at a minimum for the
procedural macro support.

Idea inspired by [this code](https://github.com/neon-bindings/neon/blob/2277e943a619579c144c1da543874f4a7ec39879/src/lib.rs#L42) in the Neon project.

## Support

This library works and [is regularly tested](https://travis-ci.org/mmastrac/rust-ctor)
on Linux, OSX and Windows, with both `+crt-static` and `-crt-static`. Other platforms are supported
but not tested as part of the automatic builds. This library will also work as expected in both
`bin` and `cdylib` outputs, ie: the `ctor` and `dtor` will run at executable or library
startup/shutdown respectively.

## Warnings

Rust's philosophy is that nothing happens before or after main and
this library explicitly subverts that. The code that runs in the `ctor`
and `dtor` functions should be careful to limit itself to `libc`
functions and code that does not rely on Rust's stdlib services.

For example, using stdout in a `dtor` function is a guaranteed panic. Consider
using the [ libc-print crate](https://crates.io/crates/libc-print) for output
to stderr/stdout during

`#[ctor]` and `#[dtor]` methods. Other issues
may involve signal processing or panic handling in that early code.In most cases, `sys_common::at_exit` is a better choice than `#[dtor]`. Caveat emptor!

On some platforms, unloading of shared libraries may not actually
happen until process exit, even if explicitly unloaded. The rules for
this are arcane and difficult to understand. For example, thread-local
storage on OSX will affect this (see [this comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/28794#issuecomment-368693049)).

## Examples

Marks the function `foo` as a module constructor, called when a static
library is loaded or an executable is started:

```
    static INITED: AtomicBool = new;

```
Creates a `HashMap` populated with strings when a static
library is loaded or an executable is started (new in `0.1.7`):

```

    /// This is an immutable static, evaluated at init time
    static STATIC_CTOR:  = ;
```
Print a message at shutdown time. Note that Rust may have shut down some stdlib services at this time.

```

    unsafe
```
## Under the Hood

The `#[ctor]` macro makes use of linker sections to ensure that a
function is run at startup time.

The above example translates into the following Rust code (approximately):

```

    static FOO: extern fn = ;
```
The `#[dtor]` macro effectively creates a constructor that calls `libc::atexit` with the provided function, ie roughly equivalent to:

```

```

# ctrlc 3.5.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ctrlc/^3.4

# CtrlC

A simple easy to use wrapper around Ctrl-C signal.

## Example usage

In `cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "3.5"
```
then, in `main.rs`

```
use channel;
use ctrlc;
```
#### Try the example yourself

`cargo build --examples && target/debug/examples/readme_example`

## Handling SIGTERM and SIGHUP

Add CtrlC to Cargo.toml using `termination` feature and CtrlC will handle SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP.

# libc 0.2.186 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libc/^0.2

# libc - Raw FFI bindings to platforms' system libraries

`libc` provides all of the definitions necessary to easily interoperate with C
code (or "C-like" code) on each of the platforms that Rust supports. This
includes type definitions (e.g. `c_int`), constants (e.g. `EINVAL`) as well as
function headers (e.g. `malloc`).

This crate exports all underlying platform types, functions, and constants under
the crate root, so all items are accessible as `libc::foo`. The types and values
of all the exported APIs match the platform that libc is compiled for.

Windows API bindings are not included in this crate. If you are looking for
WinAPI bindings, consider using crates like [windows-sys](https://docs.rs/windows-sys).

More detailed information about the design of this library can be found in its
[associated RFC](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/HEAD/text/1291-promote-libc.md).

## v1.0 Roadmap

Currently, `libc` has two active branches: `main` for the upcoming v1.0 release,
and `libc-0.2` for the currently published version. By default all pull requests
should target `main`; once reviewed, they can be cherry picked to the `libc-0.2`
branch if needed.

We will stop making new v0.2 releases once v1.0 is released.

See the section in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md#v10-roadmap) for more
details.

## Usage

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Features

-
`std`: by default`libc`links to the standard library. Disable this feature to remove this dependency and be able to use`libc`in`#![no_std]`crates.
-
`extra_traits`: all`struct`s implemented in`libc`are`Copy`and`Clone`. This feature derives`Debug`,`Eq`,`Hash`, and`PartialEq`.

The following features are deprecated:

- `use_std`: this is equivalent to- `std`
- `const-extern-fn`: this is now enabled by default
- `align`: this is now enabled by default

## Rust version support

The minimum supported Rust toolchain version is currently **Rust 1.65**.

Increases to the MSRV are allowed to change without a major (i.e. semver- breaking) release in order to avoid a ripple effect in the ecosystem. A policy for when this may change is a work in progress.

`libc` may continue to compile with Rust versions older than the current MSRV
but this is not guaranteed.

## Platform support

You can see the platform(target)-specific docs on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/libc), select a platform
you want to see.

See [ ci/verify-build.py](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/ci/verify-build.py) for
the platforms on which

`libc` is guaranteed to build for each Rust toolchain.
The test matrices at [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/actions)show the platforms in which

`libc` tests
are run.## License

This project is licensed under either of

at your option.

## Contributing

We welcome all people who want to contribute. Please see the
[contributing instructions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information.

Contributions in any form (issues, pull requests, etc.) to this project must
adhere to Rust's [Code of Conduct](https://www.rust-lang.org/policies/code-of-conduct).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted
for inclusion in `libc` by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be
dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# tempfile 3.27.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tempfile/^3

# tempfile

A secure, cross-platform, temporary file library for Rust. In addition to creating temporary files, this library also allows users to securely open multiple independent references to the same temporary file (useful for consumer/producer patterns and surprisingly difficult to implement securely).

## Usage

Minimum required Rust version: 1.63.0

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "3"
```
## Supported Platforms

This crate supports all major operating systems:

- Linux
- Android
- MacOS
- Windows
- FreeBSD (likely other BSDs but we don't have CI for them)
- RedoxOS
- Wasm (build and link only, Wasm doesn't have a filesystem)
- WASI P1 & P2.

However:

- Android, RedoxOS, Wasm, and WASI targets all require the latest stable rust compiler.
- WASI P1/P2 does not define a default temporary directory. You'll need to explicitly call `tempfile::env::override_temp_dir`with a valid directory or temporary file creation will panic on this platform.
- WASI P1/P2 does not have file permissions.
- You *may*need to override the temporary directory in Android as well to point at your application's per-app cache directory.

## Example

```
use File;
use ;
```

# phoxal-bus 0.20.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/phoxal-bus/0.20.1

# phoxal-bus

The Phoxal bus ABI floor: the Zenoh-native `bus_abi` boundary (D26/D62) plus
the two contract primitive traits ([`ApiVersion`] / [`ContractBody`]) the bus
client is generic over.

Samples are Zenoh-native: the key (`<namespace>/robots/<robot-id>/<topic>`),
an encoding string + a [`BusMetadata`] attachment (schema id, family, codec,
api version, and provenance), and a plain MessagePack body payload - there is no Phoxal frame
independent of Zenoh, and no `{"v":…}` version tag in the body (D62).

The concrete dated API versions (`y2026_1`, …) generated by the
`phoxal_api_tree!` macro - and their [`ApiVersion`] / [`ContractBody`] impls -
live in the `phoxal-api` crate (`phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …), which also re-exports
these two traits. The `phoxal` engine re-exports the typed authoring subset at
`phoxal::bus`, so the traits are also reachable as `phoxal::bus::ApiVersion` /
`phoxal::bus::ContractBody`. The raw session-opening surface lives behind the
explicit `phoxal::raw` opt-in.

---

# phoxal-bus 0.20.1 - Docs.rs

#
                    phoxal-bus 0.20.1

                Phoxal bus ABI floor: the Zenoh-native contract bus client and the API-version / contract-body primitive traits.

# arc_swap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/arc-swap/^1.9.1/

## Expand description

Making [ Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html) itself atomic

The [ ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) type is a container for an

`Arc` that can be changed atomically. Semantically,
it is similar to something like `Atomic<Arc<T>>` (if there was such a thing) or
`RwLock<Arc<T>>` (but without the need for the locking). It is optimized for read-mostly
scenarios, with consistent performance characteristics.[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

There are many situations in which one might want to have some data structure that is often read and seldom updated. Some examples might be a configuration of a service, routing tables, snapshot of some data that is renewed every few minutes, etc.

In all these cases one needs:

- Being able to read the current value of the data structure, fast, often and concurrently from many threads.
- Using the same version of the data structure over longer period of time ‒ a query should be answered by a consistent version of data, a packet should be routed either by an old or by a new version of the routing table but not by a combination, etc.
- Perform an update without disrupting the processing.

The first idea would be to use [ RwLock<T>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html) and keep a read-lock for the whole time of
processing. Update would, however, pause all processing until done.

Better option would be to have [ RwLock<Arc<T>>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html). Then one would lock, clone the

[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)and unlock. This suffers from CPU-level contention (on the lock and on the reference count of the

[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)) which makes it relatively slow. Depending on the implementation, an update may be blocked for arbitrary long time by a steady inflow of readers.

```
static ROUTING_TABLE: Lazy<RwLock<Arc<RoutingTable>>> = Lazy::new(|| {
    RwLock::new(Arc::new(RoutingTable))
});
fn process_packet(packet: Packet) {
    let table = Arc::clone(&ROUTING_TABLE.read().unwrap());
    table.route(packet);
}
```
The [ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) can be used instead, which solves the above problems and has better performance
characteristics than the [RwLock](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html), both in contended and non-contended scenarios.

```
static ROUTING_TABLE: Lazy<ArcSwap<RoutingTable>> = Lazy::new(|| {
    ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoutingTable)
});
fn process_packet(packet: Packet) {
    let table = ROUTING_TABLE.load();
    table.route(packet);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-contents)Crate contents

At the heart of the crate there are [ ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) and

[types, containers for an](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwapOption.html)

`ArcSwapOption`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)

`Arc`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)

`Option<Arc>`Technically, these are type aliases for partial instantiations of the [ ArcSwapAny](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcSwapAny.html) type. The

[is more flexible and allows tweaking of many things (can store other things than](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcSwapAny.html)

`ArcSwapAny`[s, can configure the locking](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)

`Arc`[). For details about the tweaking, see the documentation of the](https://docs.rs/strategy/trait.Strategy.html)

`Strategy`[module and the](https://docs.rs/strategy/index.html)

`strategy`[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.RefCnt.html)

`RefCnt`The [ cache](https://docs.rs/cache/index.html) module provides means for speeding up read access of the contained data at the
cost of delayed reclamation.

The [ access](https://docs.rs/access/index.html) module can be used to do projections into the contained data to separate parts
of application from each other (eg. giving a component access to only its own part of
configuration while still having it reloaded as a whole).

[§](https://docs.rs#before-using)Before using

The data structure is a bit niche. Before using, please check the
[limitations and common pitfalls](https://docs.rs/docs/limitations/index.html) and the [performance
characteristics](https://docs.rs/docs/performance/index.html), including choosing the right [read
operation](https://docs.rs/docs/performance/index.html#read-operations).

You can also get an inspiration about what’s possible in the [common patterns](https://docs.rs/docs/patterns/index.html)
section.

[§](https://docs.rs#release-19)Release 1.9

Unfortunately, several orderings were too weak in the original code (proofs based on wrong assumptions / wrong reading of the standard). The 1.9 version should fix them, but probably introduces some performance degradation.

I hope to re-design and rewrite from scratch eventually, with less amount of SeqCst needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use arc_swap::ArcSwap;
use crossbeam_utils::thread;
let config = ArcSwap::from(Arc::new(String::default()));
thread::scope(|scope| {
    scope.spawn(|_| {
        let new_conf = Arc::new("New configuration".to_owned());
        config.store(new_conf);
    });
    for _ in 0..10 {
        scope.spawn(|_| {
            loop {
                let cfg = config.load();
                if !cfg.is_empty() {
                    assert_eq!(**cfg, "New configuration");
                    return;
                }
            }
        });
    }
}).unwrap();
```
